vocabulary.example: She is proficient in three languages.

vocabulary.meaning_en: watching carefully and ready to act
changing in ways you can't guess
vocabulary.example: My boss gives me unpredictable tasks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: admit that you did something wrong
vocabulary.example: He confessed that he broke the window.

vocabulary.meaning_en: laugh at someone in a friendly, playful way
vocabulary.example: My brother likes to tease me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: decide not to continue a plan for now

vocabulary.example: Let me give you a counterargument.

vocabulary.meaning_en: put something in danger of failing
vocabulary.example: Bad planning could jeopardise the project.
It's prudent to save some money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the chance that something will happen
vocabulary.example: The odds of that happening are very small.

fine_lines.title: come clean vs pull someone's leg
fine_lines.explanation_ar: come clean = يعترف بالحقيقة. pull someone's leg = يمزح مع شخص ويخبره بشيء غير حقيقي على سبيل الدعابة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Come clean" = tell the truth. "Pull someone's leg" = joke with someone by telling them something untrue.

examples.sentence: He came clean about the mistake.
Don't worry, I was only pulling your leg.

fine_lines.title: beat around the bush vs to make a long story short
words: to make a long story short
fine_lines.explanation_ar: beat around the bush = يلفّ ويدور ولا يدخل في الموضوع. to make a long story short = يختصر ويذهب مباشرة إلى النتيجة. معنيان متعاكسان.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Beat around the bush" = avoid the main point. "To make a long story short" = go straight to the main point. They are opposites.

examples.sentence: Stop beating around the bush and tell me.

examples.word: to make a long story short
examples.sentence: To make a long story short, I missed my flight.

expressions.meaning_en: Learn how to do something after some practice.
expressions.example: It took me a while to get the hang of driving on the left.

expressions.meaning_ar: يلفّ ويدور / يتجنّب الدخول في الموضوع
expressions.example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you want.

expressions.meaning_en: Introduces something that everyone already accepts.
expressions.example: It goes without saying that a healthy diet is important.

expressions.meaning_en: Make someone stay alert and ready.
expressions.example: My boss gives me surprise tasks to keep me on my toes.

expressions.meaning_en: Tell the truth about something you did wrong.
expressions.example: I decided to come clean and apologise to my boss.
The manager turned a blind eye to his lateness.

expressions.meaning_en: Joke with someone in a friendly way.
expressions.example: I wasn't really angry. I was just pulling your leg.

expressions.phrase: to make / cut a long story short
expressions.meaning_en: Used to tell only the main point of a story.
expressions.example: To make a long story short, I got lost and missed my flight.

expressions.meaning_en: Keep someone informed about what is happening.
expressions.example: Please keep me in the loop about the new client.

expressions.meaning_en: Argue against an idea to test it, even if you agree with it.
expressions.example: Let me play devil's advocate for a minute: what if sales fall?

expressions.meaning_en: Introduces a different point after what you just said.
expressions.example: She's an excellent writer. Having said that, her speaking needs work.

expressions.meaning_en: Believing something good will happen when it probably won't.
expressions.example: Finishing everything by Friday? That's wishful thinking.

expressions.meaning_en: Tell someone about something that has been worrying you.
expressions.example: I could see he wanted to get something off his chest.

expressions.meaning_en: Talk about the most important thing without delay.
expressions.example: Let me get straight to the point: we need more time.

grammar.title: Having said that = However
grammar.explanation_ar: Having said that رابط يعني however (ومع ذلك). يأتي في بداية الجملة الثانية ليقدّم رأيًا مختلفًا أو تحفظًا.
grammar.explanation_en: "Having said that" is a linker meaning "however". It starts the next sentence and adds a different view.
examples: The plan looks great. Having said that, it's expensive.
He's very clever. Having said that, he's often late.
I love summer. Having said that, I hate the heat.

grammar.title: It goes without saying + that-clause
grammar.explanation_ar: It goes without saying يأتي بعدها that + جملة كاملة.
grammar.explanation_en: "It goes without saying" is followed by "that" + a full clause.
examples: It goes without saying that we'll pay you for overtime.
It goes without saying that safety comes first.
It goes without saying that you should be careful with money.

questions.question: "After a few weeks, I got the hang of it" means:
choices: I hung it on the wall.
I learnt how to do it.
questions.explanation_ar: get the hang of = يتقن بعد التدرّب.
questions.explanation_en: "Get the hang of" = learn how to do it.

questions.question: Stop ___ around the bush and tell me the news!
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير هو beat around the bush.
questions.explanation_en: The idiom is "beat around the bush".

questions.question: "The teacher turned a blind eye" means the teacher:
questions.explanation_en: It means pretended not to notice.

questions.question: "I was just pulling your leg" means:
questions.explanation_en: It means I was only joking.

questions.question: Please keep me ___ the loop about the project.
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير الصحيح: keep someone in the loop (يُبقيه على اطّلاع).

questions.question: Which expression means "tell the truth about a mistake"?
"We'll finish it all by lunchtime." — "That's ___." (It's very unlikely.)
"Having said that" is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation_ar: Having said that تعني however (ومع ذلك).

questions.question: Someone argues against a plan just to test it. They are:
questions.explanation_ar: play devil's advocate = يلعب دور المعارض لاختبار الفكرة.

questions.question: Firefighters must always be ready. They are always ___.
